FINDINGS OUTSIDE THE CLAIMS

F1 — the new `RangeError` sentence ships as an ungated behavioural prose claim, in the published README.
Where: /home/user/fleet/ndjson/README.md:25-26 ("past the host's maximum string length the buffer append throws a `RangeError`, and the cap is what prevents it") and /home/user/fleet/ndjson/guides/ndjson.md:23-24 (the same clause).
What is wrong: `.claude/rules/documentation.md` § Parity requires that "Where a prose claim about behavior sits under no fence, add the executed assertion that would break if the claim went false." Neither sentence sits under a fence, and no gated project asserts the throw. A grep for `RangeError|MAX_STRING|maximum string` over the package excluding `node_modules` returns only these two prose sites plus an unrelated JSON-nesting comment at tests/src/core/NDJSONParser.test.ts:614. The only executed proof is /home/user/fleet/ndjson/tmp/probe/buffer.test.ts, which `.gitignore:11` ignores, no gate collects, and the retention rule sweeps at acceptance.
Why it matters: this is the same rule that generated ndjson-obj-1. The round removed one unfalsifiable prose claim from README.md:6 and replaced part of it with a second unfalsifiable prose claim in the same file, which reaches every consumer who installs the package. `README.md` is in `package.json:20-23`'s `files` list, so the ungated sentence is published.
This is not a fault of the writer against its rows: ndjson-obj-3 prescribed this exact prose and ruled that the measurement is recorded in the commit message. The obligation attaches to the sentence that shipped, so it belongs to a successor unit rather than to a re-dispatch of this one.
What right looks like — option, cost, recommendation. Option A: commit the probe's second case into tests/src/core/NDJSONParser.test.ts beside the existing adversarial pin at :609-627, without the `console.log` lines and without a `node:*` import, doubling a string until the append throws and asserting `RangeError`. Cost: roughly 512 MB peak allocation inside the `src:core` project, heavier than the depth pin already there, and it must be re-run alone before any red reading is believed. Option B: keep the sentence in guides/ndjson.md and drop it from the published README. Cost: the guide's claim is still ungated, and README.md:6's narrowed never-throws sentence loses the qualifier that made it honest. Recommendation: Option A. It is the only one that closes the rule; Option B only bounds the exposure.

F2 — the retained report states counts, which `AGENTS.md` § Writing bans in prose everywhere.
Where: /home/user/scaffold/tmp/units/conform/conform-ndjson-report.md:12 ("All six package-owned `AGENTS §N` pointers deleted"), :10 ("still used at three sites in that file"), and :131 ("Three ancillary decisions, recorded").
What is wrong: each number answers "how many" about a set that can grow — pointers, call sites, decisions — and the rule is "Name the members, or write the sentence without the number. Delete a count you find. Do not correct it."
Why it matters: the report is a durable artifact retained under `.orkestrel/ndjson/`, and a successor unit reads it as this campaign's record.
What right looks like: :12 → "Every package-owned `AGENTS §N` pointer deleted, sentences kept."; :10 → "`BACKSLASH` kept, still used in that file."; :131 → "Ancillary decisions, recorded:".
